text: Cantor's theorem states that |A| < |𝒫(A)| for every set A. Its proof shows that no function f: A → 𝒫(A) can be surjective by exhibiting which set?
choices: The union ⋃A of all elements of A
The diagonal set D = {x ∈ A : x ∉ f(x)}
explanation: The diagonal set D = {x ∈ A : x ∉ f(x)} is a subset of A (so D ∈ 𝒫(A)) that differs from every value f(y): if y ∈ D then y ∉ f(y), and if y ∉ D then y ∈ f(y), so f(y) ≠ D always. Hence f is not onto. The other sets do not produce the diagonal contradiction.
